name: Quick coding suite
description: Three small, discriminating tasks (greenfield code, bug fix, arithmetic reasoning) run headless across Claude, Codex, Gemini and OpenCode/MiniMax.

tasks.title: Parse durations
tasks.prompt:
In the current directory, create `duration.py` with a function `parse_duration(text: str) -> int` that returns a duration in whole seconds.

Rules:
- Units are `h`, `m`, `s` (case-insensitive), each used at most once, in that order (h before m before s).
- Each unit is preceded by a non-negative integer. Components may be separated by single spaces; leading/trailing whitespace is ignored.
- Examples: `45s` -> 45, `2h` -> 7200, `1h30m` -> 5400, `1h 5m 3s` -> 3903, `90m` -> 5400.
- Anything else (empty string, unknown unit, missing number or unit, decimals, negatives, repeated or out-of-order units) raises `ValueError`.

Also create `test_duration.py` with `unittest` tests (standard library only) covering valid and invalid input. Do not ask questions; just write the files and make sure `python3 -m unittest` passes.

tasks.title: Fix slugify
Shipping arithmetic
tasks.prompt: A warehouse ships 120 boxes on Monday. Every following day it ships 15% fewer boxes than the previous day, rounded down to a whole box. How many boxes does it ship in total from Monday through Friday? Show brief working, then end with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <integer>`. Do not create any files.
